title: Decoupling the Brain from the Hands: Claude Managed Agents (Part 1 of 4) — Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic engineers describe rebuilding Claude Managed Agents from a single-container 'pet' architecture into three decoupled interfaces: an append-only session event log, an interchangeable harness/brain, and on-demand sandbox 'hands'. They also cover credential proxying, flexible compaction over the raw event log, and faster time-to-first-token by starting inference before sandbox spin-up.

takeaways.technique: Decouple brain (harness/loop) from hands (sandbox) via append-only event log
takeaways.what_they_do: Session state is an append-only event log; the harness and sandbox are disposable and resume by replaying the log from the last event, so a dead sandbox or harness is just restarted rather than nursed back.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the harness died, you could bring up a new instance of the harness and continue where you left off by essentially just reading your event log

takeaways.technique: Credential proxy so secrets never enter the sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Sandbox calls that need a token route through a proxy that injects the credential at the external endpoint, so the model never sees tokens and prompt injection cannot exfiltrate them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: credentials never entered our sandbox ... it would be routed through a proxy that would inject your token before it called the external endpoint

takeaways.technique: Keep raw event log, make compaction a read-time strategy
takeaways.what_they_do: Nothing is discarded from the session log; compaction decides at read time whether to summarize the whole log or take the last N events, keeping context strategy swappable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: nothing is ever thrown away ... the compaction strategy is the one that's deciding oh do I want to look at my entire event log

takeaways.technique: Start inference before sandbox is ready; spawn sandbox lazily
takeaways.what_they_do: The brain begins the model call immediately and only provisions the sandbox when a tool actually needs it, instead of blocking on container spin-up before the first token.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cloud would only spawn the sandbox when it needed and it would not wait for the container sandbox to spin up for you to get your first token back

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness can call a sandbox container, a customer VPC, or an MCP server as interchangeable 'hands', so new execution targets plug in without changing the agent loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one brain can reach many hands ... all these like hands are essentially interchangeable

takeaways.technique: Treat harness assumptions as model-specific and versioned
takeaways.what_they_do: Harness workarounds encode assumptions about a specific model (e.g. context-anxiety resets for Sonnet 4.5) that go stale on the next model, so they design interfaces to outlast assumptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: harnesses encode assumptions and assumptions can go stale ... we designed interfaces to outlast these assumptions
